title: Scale controller throttling caused invisible queue buildup and customer-facing errors
creator: Ava Chen
description: Several enterprise customers reported increased 429/503s and elevated tail latency during regional traffic spikes. Investigation shows the scale-controller began applying a throttle window on allocation requests which caused requests to queue in an internal admission buffer; the buffer had no observable metric surfaced to console, so operator dashboards and automatic fallback policies did not trigger. This ticket tracks root cause, mitigation, and long-term guardrails to prevent invisible queueing and reserved-pool shortfalls.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a reserved pool with warmup credit=30s and headroom=10% to staging region
2) Generate a synthetic microburst pattern (1000 rps sustained for 90s, with 3x spikes every 10s) against a tenant pinned to that pool
3) Observe scale-controller logs for throttle windows and allocation rate limiting
4) Correlate admission buffer length (internal queue) with increase in 429s from the serving runtime
5) Reproduce with feature-flag disabled (throttle off) to validate behavior disappears
investigation_notes: Telemetry: allocation-api returned 429/RateLimited for ~3s windows during scale-controller leader churn (k8s node restarts) — manifested as bursty rejections downstream.

Admission buffer: a new admission queue optimization (PR #1789) was added to smooth allocation bursts; it had a hard limit of 500 pending requests but no metrics emitted when near-capacity and no circuit-breaker to trigger fallback routing.
Leader election: during scale-controller leader handoff we observed delayed cache warmup causing conservative throttle policy (backoffMultiplier ramped from 1 to 8).

Mismatch: console alerts only monitor pool.AvailableSlots and eps-drop, not admission queue length; automated fallbacks rely on pool.AvailableSlots which remained non-zero until the admission queue overflowed, so users saw throttling before failover to compatible variants kicked in.
Customer impact: three customers in EU region experienced degraded throughput for 7–12 minutes each; two opened escalations and one support ticket led to on-call paging.
PR and commits: revert candidate PR (commit 0a1b2c) and add defensive metrics in PR #1794.
root_cause_summary: A recent admission buffering optimization introduced an in-memory queue without observable telemetry or a gate to force fallback when the queue saturated. Combined with leader-election induced throttle ramps in the scale-controller, allocation requests were delayed and occasionally rejected, causing silent capacity shortfalls despite pool.AvailableSlots appearing adequate. In short: invisible admission queue + conservative throttle during leadership churn = customer-facing tail errors.
mitigation_plan: Immediate: roll back the admission-buffering change in staging and progressively to EU (hotpatch PR #1796). Short-term: expose admission_queue_length metric and add alert (console-telemetry ticket). Implement a conservative circuit-breaker that forces fallback routing when admission_queue_length > 70% of capacity. Long-term: rework throttle policy to be leader-change aware and add leader_warmup_grace duration so the controller does not apply aggressive ramp multipliers during election windows.
rollout_plan: 1) Hotpatch EU region with admission-buffer revert (canary 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) over 60m, monitor 5s token-level latency and 429 rate; 2) Deploy metrics and alerting to console (alpha dashboards) in parallel; 3) Deploy circuit-breaker patch with feature flag toggled off initially and enabled after smoke-tests; 4) Ship leader-aware throttle policy in next minor release runtime-1.21.
test_plan: Add unit tests for admission buffer overflow handling
E2E test that simulates leader election while driving high allocation rates
Chaos test: orchestrate controller pod restart in staging during synthetic bursts and verify fallback routes activate
Load test: confirm no regression on cold-start latency for small tenants
communication: Customer comms drafted: EU customers affected notified via support with root cause summary and ETA for full fix
Status page: minor degradation posted during incident window; follow-up update scheduled after hotpatch rollout
Internal: PagerDuty incident runbook updated with step to disable admission buffer via runtime flag
notes: Decision trade-offs: reverting admission buffer reduces batching efficiency for short windows but restores observability and safe fallbacks. We'll reintroduce a version of buffering with persistent metrics and backpressure semantics rather than silent enqueueing.
Monitoring gaps: add admission_queue_length to per-pool telemetry and create an automated test that asserts metric emits under synthetic load
Follow-ups: create PM ticket to review SLOs for reserved pools and update SLA communication for tiered fallbacks
